title: Long-audio Analysis CPU duty-cycle / overlapping spectral-work thermal-risk hardening

production_changes.tempo: Ordinary audio below 1800 seconds keeps historical per-frame rescan summation order. Long audio uses rolling sum-of-squares with an exact ring-window rebase every 2048 natural Tempo frames.
production_changes.chord: Hann weights, MIDI frequencies, Goertzel coefficients and windowed scratch are created once per Analysis accumulator and reused. Chord cadence, Goertzel recurrence, candidate scoring, vocabulary and confidence logic remain unchanged.
production_changes.mismatch_behavior: Reusable Chord workspace falls back to legacy ChordFrameClassifier if sample count or sample rate does not match the precomputed kernel.

tempo_microbenchmark.note: Portable Tempo energy-path microbenchmark only; not physical-iPhone thermal or battery evidence.

chord_microbenchmark.note: The modest wall reduction is expected because the 48 x window Goertzel recurrence remains unchanged.

limitations: The 1800-second Tempo switch is a CPU-resource implementation boundary, not a quality/PARITY threshold.
Rolling Tempo energy is mathematically equivalent but not bit-identical to repeated floating-point rescan between periodic exact rebases; ordinary-song paths remain on the old summation order.
Chord reuse removes repeated setup transcendental work and scratch allocation but deliberately does not alter the dominant Goertzel recurrence, chord cadence or classification semantics.
Portable Linux timings do not establish physical-iPhone thermal, battery or wall-time acceptance.
MOI-P021 remains MISSING until genuine Lane-2 bounded decode and HQ W23/W24 physical-iPhone acceptance are completed.
P009/P011/P013/P016 remain subject to rights-cleared W22 differential and current-iPhone Moises evidence.
